source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade and Downgrade HIB-CPLD firmware by Redfish when system is booted
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish REST client, on the BMC side) + HIB-CPLD image (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- HIB-CPLD downgrade via Redfish (system is booted): the agent needs the exact user-provided HIB-CPLD image first the SUT must be booted first and the host OS running for the flash, then runs the Redfish update flow: `PATCH /redfish/v1/UpdateService` (set preserve/replace behavior), `POST /redfish/v1/UpdateService` to upload the image, poll the returned TaskService task to completion, then `GET /redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory` to confirm the new version is active. Not a single one-liner; run step-by-step after the image is placed on the BMC.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the full Redfish PATCH/POST response, the TaskService poll loop, and the final `FirmwareInventory` JSON so the user confirms the HIB-CPLD version changed, only one BMC reset happened, and the SUT still boots/passes self-checks.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: HIB-CPLD firmware flash via Redfish is state-changing and can brick the BMC/host if interrupted; flash only the user-specified image with host powered off for a clean result, and never interrupt mid-flash.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; treats the target as HIB-CPLD but assumes generic UpdateService/task semantics and contradicts the booted-host state in its risk text.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED; identifies the reset/host-state/security gaps but does not foreground the HIB-CPLD Items versus FPGA Procedure mismatch.
historical_reviews.round_02: YES; entry 719/2291 preserves the row for manual reconciliation.

original_test_intent: Intended to upgrade and downgrade HIB-CPLD firmware through Redfish while the host is booted, but the Procedure instead commands an FPGA firmware operation and the reset/host-state contract is also inconsistent.
original_method: The source PATCHes Immediate apply, POSTs an unspecified image to an assumed UpdateService URI, waits for completion, performs an undefined single BMC reset, and reads FirmwareInventory.
manual_activity: The owner must select the actual target component and operating/reset state; an authorized engineer approves the resulting destructive plan and recovery before agent execution can be reconsidered.
required_inputs: Decision whether target is HIB-CPLD or FPGA
safety_requirements: Do not send an image while Items and Procedure identify different components.
Do not use embedded credentials, `curl -k`, an assumed `/update` URI or unverified Immediate apply.
Never retry, reverse direction or add resets after an uncertain write.
Require stable power and independent BMC/component/host recovery; preserve raw errors.
agent_execution_scope: After correction, discover the target capability and execute one immutable, approved API transition at a time with terminal task and independent activation evidence.
Do not write firmware, reset the BMC or set a formal verdict while target and state semantics conflict.
engineer_actions: Correct the component identity and align Items, Procedure, script and expected inventory evidence.
Define transition/reset/host-state contract, approve security/recovery and issue final verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its HIB-CPLD interpretation follows Items but cannot repair the source Procedure's explicit FPGA operation; its powered-off risk also conflicts with the booted test.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No write command is valid until the component is corrected. Then use only the target-advertised, vendor-approved action through trusted TLS and protected credentials.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The conflicting HIB-CPLD Items/FPGA Procedure, supplied PATCH/POST/GET, booted wording, 10/30-minute values and one-reset criterion remain verbatim.

modernized_recommendation.status: PENDING COMPONENT AND STATE CONTRACT CORRECTION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correct the target first, then bind a signed image to that component and advertised action, capture terminal update status, account for the approved reset and verify active inventory plus host/BMC/component health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the corrected named component on a confirmed BMC service.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record Redfish schema/service, BMC, component image and client versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor documentation for the corrected component update, activation and recovery path.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Would remove the component mismatch, unsafe authentication and assumed endpoint while preserving both transition directions.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Prevents flashing the wrong programmable device and adds deterministic activation/health evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: HIB-CPLD and FPGA are not interchangeable targets; no generic command may bridge the conflict.

project_override_considerations: Project inputs may select versions and a vendor action after the Master source target is corrected; an override cannot silently redefine HIB-CPLD as FPGA.
expected_evidence: Approved source correction naming one component
Advertised action and redacted API/task transcript
Exact approved reset and host-state timeline
Pre/post active component inventory and host/BMC health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Script name HIB-CPLD, while the Procedure explicitly says FPGA firmware. The source and same-row risk also disagree on booted versus powered-off host state, and the sole BMC reset has no initiator/timing definition.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Component identity determines the destructive target; it cannot be inferred from a generic image variable. The additional host/reset ambiguities prevent a safe state machine, so this is irreducibly blocked pending correction.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Its HIB-CPLD assumption is not accepted as a source correction, and its endpoint/task/host-state assumptions are rejected.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED but strengthens the basis with the explicit HIB-CPLD-versus-FPGA conflict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Distinguishes true target ambiguity from ordinary missing versions or packages.

review_improvement: Prevents a firmware image from being directed at the wrong programmable component and enumerates the exact source corrections needed.
independent_technical_reasoning: A Redfish firmware flow is software-automatable only after the target is deterministic. Here the authoritative source names two different hardware targets and incompatible host-state guidance, so automation readiness cannot be safely established.
